x: Exam key: PARAM Siddhi-AI, which entered the TOP500 at rank 62/63 (Nov 2020) and was India's highest-ranked system then. Strictly, the first Indian system in the TOP500 was PARAM Padma (June 2003, rank 171); PARAM 8000 and 10000 never entered it.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercomputing_in_India (PARAM Padma first Indian system on a world fastest list, June 2003); drishtiias.com/daily-updates/daily-news-analysis/supercomputer-param-siddhi (PARAM Siddhi-AI 63rd in TOP500, Nov 2020)
dispute: Exam key: PARAM Siddhi-AI (India's top TOP500 entry, 63rd in Nov 2020). Strictly: PARAM Padma was the first Indian system on the TOP500, June 2003 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercomputing_in_India).

x: Official key: 9.2 W/m². India's limits (from 1 Sept 2012) are one-tenth of ICNIRP – 0.45 W/m² at 900 MHz and 0.90 W/m² at 1800 MHz; 9.0-9.2 W/m² is the ICNIRP level at 1800 MHz. (Moved to telecom.)
source: DoT presentation, ITU EMF workshop 2013 (https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-T/climatechange/emf-1305/Documents/Presentations/s2part2p3-RKBhatnagar.pdf) slide 6: ICNIRP 4.5/9.0/10.5 W/m² vs DoT 0.45/0.90/1.05 W/m² from 01.09.2012
evidence: ITU/DoT presentation slide 6 (opened PDF): 900 MHz 0.45, 1800 MHz 0.90, 2100 MHz 1.05 W/m² (1/10th of ICNIRP) from 01.09.2012
web search: DoT documents/court affidavit 0.45, 0.9, 1 W/m²; DoT study paper July 2022 (403, not opened)
dispute: Official key: 9.2 watt/m². Strictly: India's limit is 1/10th of ICNIRP – 0.90 W/m² at 1800 MHz (0.45 at 900 MHz); about 9 W/m² is the ICNIRP level (DoT presentation, ITU 2013, slide 6).

x: The printed key takes liquid oxygen as 'not a propellant' because it is the oxidiser, not a fuel. In fact LH2, LOX, hydrazine and kerosene (RP-1) all serve as rocket propellants.
source: NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 (src/science-tech/nextgen-st-group2-02.txt) p.10-11 (propellant = fuel + oxidizer; LOX the oxidizer of cryogenic stages); printed key, not verified
dispute: Printed key: (b) liquid oxygen. Strictly: all four are used; LOX is a propellant component (oxidiser) (NextGen S&T G2 Part 2 p.10-11; PMF S&T Part 1 p.137).
evidence: web search: RAS 2018 paper/official key not found; Britannica/Wikipedia: LH2, LOX, hydrazine, RP-1 all used

x: Artemis III was announced as NASA's first crewed landing near the lunar south pole (then 2025); Pioneer 1-3 were 1958 probes. In 2026 NASA made Artemis III a 2027 Earth-orbit test, and the landing moved to Artemis IV (2028) (now Artemis IV).
outdated: ⚠ Outdated: NASA restructured Artemis in 2026 — now Artemis III is a 2027 low-Earth-orbit lander docking test and Artemis IV (2028) the first crewed south-pole landing (Rocket CA 2026 Part 2 p.93-94; Drishti IAS 15 Jun 2026)

x: China was the first foreign buyer of the Russian S-400 (Rosoboronexport, April 2015; deliveries from 2018); Turkey and India followed. Belarus announced its S-400 purchase only in May 2022, so the stem's 'after Russia and Belarus' is loose, but China is the only fitting option.
source: https://www.armyrecognition.com/archives/archives-land-defense/land-defense-2015/china-becomes-first-foreign-buyer-of-russian-s-400-air-defense-system-according-media (13 Apr 2015: China first buyer); https://missilethreat.csis.org/belarus-buys-iskander-missiles-and-s-400-anti-missile-systems-from-russia (Belarus purchase announced 19 May 2022)
evidence: armyrecognition.com 13 Apr 2015 (Rosoboronexport: China first buyer; Belarus only 'interested')
missilethreat.csis.org Belarus buys Iskander and S-400 (19 May 2022)
dispute: Key: China (first foreign S-400 buyer). Strictly: Belarus announced its S-400 purchase only in May 2022, after China (2018), Turkey (2019) and India (2021) (CSIS Missile Threat).

evidence: PMF S&T Part 4 p.31 and p.25
no source in src/ mentions Cobalt-62
dispute: Printed key: Cobalt-62 (misprint). Strictly: Cobalt-60 is the cancer-therapy isotope (PMF S&T Part 4 p.31).

from_notes: The amendment aims to phase out the use of potent greenhouse gases called hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), widely used in air conditioners.
x: The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol phases down HFCs. India (Group 2) has a 2024-26 baseline, freezes in 2028 and cuts 85% by 2047 (the stem's 2045 is the Group 1 date).
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.2 (src/environment/nextgen-environment-appsc-14.txt) p.6; UNEP Ozone Secretariat, Kigali Amendment tenth-anniversary briefing (ozone.unep.org/.../KA@10-briefing.pdf): Article 5 Group 2 baseline 2024-26, freeze 2028, 85% cut by 2047
evidence: NextGen Environment Part 8.2 p.6 ('80-85% ... by 2045', general)
UNEP Ozone Secretariat KA@10 briefing (opened PDF): Group 2 85% by 2047; Group 1 80% by 2045
